solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Somehow racist Sam fills important post

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of these three words get put together in some new, unspecified way

explanation.surface: A bigot called Sam lands a significant job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fills' looks like the link to the definition, but it is part of the fodder: RACIST SAM FILLS gives fourteen letters, the whole answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail sent at the higher, faster Royal Mail rate is the most important category of post.

clue.text: Drug found when pub on fire put out

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or upset, so these words have their letters disordered

explanation.surface: Painkillers turn up after a pub blaze is extinguished.
explanation.definitionFit: A common over-the-counter anti-inflammatory painkiller is a drug.

clue.text: Rigid back end

definitions.meaning: rigid here means strict or unbending in manner
the back end of a boat or ship

explanation.definitionFit: Stern means strict or severe, and also the rear part of a ship.

clue.text: Ronaldo, man respected, pulled up during tumultuous action

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the other, here inside the jumbled letters
tumultuous means wild and disorderly, so the word action is rearranged
in a down clue, pulled up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Sir is the title of a respected man, a knight

explanation.surface: A footballer performs in the thick of frenetic play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man respected' means a knight, whose title is used as a mark of respect; 'pulled up' reverses it in this down clue and 'tumultuous' scrambles the word action around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Portuguese footballer Ronaldo has the first name Cristiano.

clue.text: Indian potato fellow finds cold

parts.note: aloo is the Hindi word for potato, familiar from curry menus

explanation.surface: A chap discovers that Indian spuds have gone cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone distant and unfriendly in manner is described as cold or standoffish.

clue.text: Goodness moi?

parts.note: a French speaker, using the French word for me, would exclaim something different for 'Goodness'

explanation.surface: A startled exclamation with a touch of Miss Piggy.
explanation.definitionFit: This French oath is an exclamation of surprise, the equivalent of 'goodness me'.

clue.text: Excellent oil mixed with mayonnaise

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as A and I

indicators.note: mixed tells us the letters of oil are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Good oil blended into a mayonnaise.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (excellent) is read with the digit 1 as the letter I, then OLI comes from OIL rearranged by 'mixed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlic mayonnaise from Provence is a kind of mayonnaise.

clue.text: Food discovered at bend in road

indicators.note: in says the one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road
to sag is to bend or droop

explanation.surface: Something to eat is found at a curve in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian baked pasta dish is a food.

clue.text: Composer found in tavern, on beer, somewhat exhausted

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: a bar is a tavern

indicators.note: somewhat exhausted means partly used up, so beer loses one of its letters

explanation.surface: A musician is found in the pub after one beer too many.
explanation.walkthrough: BEER minus one E leaves BER. Samuel Barber was an American composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Barber, who wrote the Adagio for Strings, was a composer.

clue.text: Recreate morning service

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem
use means service, as in 'of service' or 'of use'

explanation.surface: Restage a church service held in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recreate' looks like 'create again', but it means to entertain, as in recreation.
explanation.definitionFit: To recreate in the older sense is to divert or entertain, which is a synonym.

clue.text: European award makes press angry

parts.note: to iron is to press clothes
cross means angry

explanation.surface: A European prize gets the newspapers riled.
explanation.definitionFit: This German military decoration is an award from a European country.

clue.text: Nobleman gets right one club admission

indicators.note: a club's admission of something takes it inside, so the club word goes around the rest

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aristocrat gains entry to a club through the right connections.
explanation.definitionFit: A holder of a hereditary title ranking below a baron is a member of the nobility, loosely a nobleman.

clue.text: Chuck pens similar notes with emotion

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so one piece is written around the other

parts.note: to fling is to chuck or throw
two of the same musical note, E and E

explanation.surface: Chuck writes matching letters with real passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like a man's name writing with pens, but it is the verb throw and the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling is an emotion, such as joy or anger.

clue.text: Hand over for decision that may go either way

indicators.note: a word that may go either way reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Pass a close call up to a higher authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may go either way' looks like part of the definition, a decision that is uncertain, but it says the word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a matter to someone else to decide on is to submit it, a synonym.

clue.text: Rise and Fall here charted?

parts.note: reads like a history of an empire, but means the rises and falls of land shown on a chart

explanation.surface: A chronicle of how an empire grew and collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: A map showing hills and valleys in three dimensions charts the rise and fall of the land.

clue.text: Slice taken by theatrical investor?

parts.note: a theatre backer is an angel, so the share such a backer takes is jokingly a slice of their kind of cake

explanation.surface: A stage backer claims a share of the takings.
explanation.definitionFit: A light sponge cake shares its first word with the theatrical term for a show's financial backer.

clue.text: Elderly doing well

definitions.meaning: elderly means advanced in years, growing old
doing well means making progress or succeeding

explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means growing old, and also means progressing or succeeding.

clue.text: May be too late for this clown!

definitions.text: May be too late for this clown!

parts.words: May be too late for this clown!
parts.note: May is the month, which comes after the first of the previous month when pranks are played

explanation.surface: A warning that time is running out to catch a joker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tricked on the first of the month before May is called a fool, a kind of clown.

clue.text: Select from group with record on the shelves

parts.note: a single is a record with one song
a record that is out has been released and is in the shops

explanation.surface: Picking from a band's catalogue a record on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick one person from a group is to select them specially.

clue.text: During crime hard to understand commotion

indicators.note: During puts the second piece within the first

parts.note: a sin is an offence or crime
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to dig is slang for to understand

explanation.surface: A crime so tricky to grasp it causes uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is a noisy party or a row, hence a commotion.

clue.text: Doug Richmond holds tongue

indicators.note: holds says the answer is contained within the name

explanation.surface: Mr Richmond keeps his mouth shut.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue here is a language: Ugric is a branch of the Finno-Ugric family including Hungarian.

clue.text: One looking after sick keeps engineering job

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a carer looks after the sick or infirm
E is the abbreviation for engineering

explanation.surface: A nurse keeps a job in engineering.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is a job or profession.

clue.text: Disorder where international students seen by head

parts.note: L is a learner driver, so two students give LL
a ness is a headland, a head

explanation.surface: Sickness among overseas students seen by the headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness is a disease or disorder of the body.

clue.text: See through constellation's flimsy fabric

indicators.note: through puts one piece passing inside the other

parts.note: Lyra is the constellation of the Lyre
the letter C is pronounced like the word see

explanation.surface: A see-through gauzy material printed with stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See through' looks like transparent, but See gives C and through is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretchy synthetic material used in sportswear is a thin, light fabric.

clue.text: This primary character in Matrix destroyed?

definitions.text: This primary character in Matrix destroyed?

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
the primary character is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Asking which leading figure in The Matrix meets his end.
explanation.walkthrough: Agent Smith, the films' villain, is destroyed at the end of the trilogy, so the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Agent Smith is a principal character in The Matrix films and is finally destroyed.

clue.text: Ireland, wherein politician has drink for murderous stakeholder

indicators.note: wherein means inside which, so the following pieces go inside Ireland's letters

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: An Irish politician has a drink while wielding a stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stakeholder' looks like a business investor, but it is someone who holds a stake to kill with, like Vlad the Impaler.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who kills by driving a stake through victims is a murderer holding a stake.

clue.text: Zeppelin man's factories

definitions.meaning: Robert ... was the singer of the rock band Led Zeppelin

explanation.definitionFit: Robert Plant sang with Led Zeppelin; plants are factories or industrial works.

clue.text: Cured by German, pandemic suddenly going away

indicators.note: cured means treated or processed, so the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A German treatment ends a pandemic abruptly.
explanation.definitionFit: Decamping is leaving hurriedly or abruptly, often secretly.

clue.text: Solo for boy on vibraphone at last

parts.note: Al is a boy's name, short for Alan or Albert
taken as written

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A solo for a boy playing vibraphone at the end of a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something solo is doing it alone, without anyone else.

clue.text: Pester at length perhaps to take tough decision

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Nagging someone at great length to make them face facts.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp the nettle is an idiom meaning to tackle a difficult matter boldly.
